candidates.title: AI ontologies for spiritual aging
candidates.shift: Researchers are using topic-modeling AI (BERTopic) to formalize 'gerotranscendence' and solitude into a machine-readable ontology, turning a soft psychological/spiritual concept into structured knowledge infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: signals encoding subjective spiritual/psychological states into AI-legible ontologies — an odd convergence of gerontology, esoteric self-development language, and machine learning infrastructure.
candidates.evidence: Paper uses BERTopic modeling for concept discovery to build an ontology of gerotranscendence and solitude, reducing manual ontology-building bias.
candidates.initial_analysis: Early example of formalizing subjective/spiritual human experience into machine ontologies, driven by AI's need for structured knowledge in eldercare; if scaled, aging-related spiritual frameworks could become quantified within care-tech systems.
candidates.author: B. Damayanthi Jesudas, Finn Wilson, Rachel A. Mavrovich et al.

candidates.title: Grassroots 'anti-monuments' as counter-memory infrastructure
candidates.shift: Civil society in Mexico is erecting unauthorized 'antimonumentos' marking state violence and femicide, creating a parallel, contested memorial landscape outside official commemorative practice.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a bottom-up reframing of memorial/funerary practice as protest infrastructure — could presage more DIY, contested monument movements as trust in state memory-making erodes.
candidates.evidence: Atlas Obscura profile of Mexico City's antimonumentos, grassroots markers protesting organized-crime violence and human rights abuses.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from state-controlled to citizen-authored public memory, driven by distrust in institutions; if it spreads, cities could see growing informal memorial infrastructures contesting official narratives.

candidates.title: Papier-mâché craft as living devotional infrastructure
candidates.shift: Traditional Mexican cartonería (papier-mâché) craftsmanship continues to be used for functioning altarpieces, blending folk-art economics with religious practice.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: artisanal craft revival intersecting with devotional infrastructure — worth watching as craft economies market heritage techniques as both art and functional ritual objects.
candidates.evidence: Atlas Obscura piece on a papier-mâché altarpiece at Plaza Capuchinas, describing cartonería as a major Mexico City folk-art tradition.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of craft-revival economics where traditional handcraft persists as functional religious infrastructure rather than pure tourism decoration; could inform how heritage crafts sustain relevance through ritual utility.

candidates.title: Japan builds forensic social work from scratch
candidates.shift: Japan is developing forensic social work as a formal interdisciplinary field bridging law and social services, currently in 'infancy' despite rising demand.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an institutional field being invented in real time in a non-Anglophone context — early indicator of how justice-adjacent professions localize differently outside Western models.
candidates.evidence: Journal of Forensic Social Work paper describing the field in Japan as emerging, interdisciplinary, and educationally underdeveloped despite growing demand.
candidates.initial_analysis: Signals professionalization of a legal-social hybrid field in a country historically resistant to Western institutional imports; if it matures, expect new credentialing bodies and shifts in handling justice-involved populations.
candidates.author: Hiroki Toi

candidates.title: Narco-capital accumulation as parallel political economy
candidates.shift: A structural-historical analysis frames Latin American drug economies as a distinct 'narcocapital accumulation' cycle entrenched within global capitalism, not just a crime problem.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: reframes narcotrafficking as an institutionalized economic-political system with its own class structure — a lens that could reshape how foresight treats shadow economies.
candidates.evidence: Revista Mexicana paper using panel data (2013-2022) analyzing narcocapital accumulation cycles, inequality, and impunity across Latin America.
candidates.source: Revista Mexicana de Ciencias Políticas y Sociales
candidates.initial_analysis: Reframes organized crime from episodic violence to structural political economy; if this framing gains traction, policy could shift from criminal-justice responses toward economic/class-based interventions in shadow economies.
candidates.author: J. Guijarro
